construct: Pathogenic variants in genes such as AGPAT2 or BSCL2 impair adipocyte development or function and prevent normal storage of triglyceride in adipose tissue. The resulting near-total loss of body fat causes ectopic lipid deposition, hypertriglyceridemia, insulin resistance/diabetes, and fatty liver.

distractor_audit.rationale: Familial hypercholesterolemia causes markedly elevated LDL cholesterol and premature atherosclerosis, not near-total absence of adipose tissue with ectopic fat storage and severe insulin resistance.
Glycogen storage disease type I produces fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, and metabolic abnormalities but does not cause congenital generalized loss of adipose tissue.
Cushing syndrome causes centripetal fat accumulation rather than a congenital near-total absence of adipose tissue.
Prader-Willi syndrome is characterized by hyperphagia and obesity rather than generalized congenital lipodystrophy.

educational_objective_text: Recognize congenital generalized lipodystrophy from near-total loss of adipose tissue with a muscular appearance, hypertriglyceridemia, insulin resistance, and hepatomegaly.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Near-total loss of adipose tissue from infancy with a muscular appearance, hepatomegaly, acanthosis nigricans, severe hypertriglyceridemia, and hyperglycemia is the characteristic metabolic phenotype of congenital generalized lipodystrophy.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: GSD I can cause hepatomegaly and hyperlipidemia but characteristically causes fasting hypoglycemia and does not cause congenital generalized lipoatrophy. Familial hypercholesterolemia centers on markedly elevated cholesterol/LDL and premature coronary disease; Cushing syndrome increases central/upper-body fat; Prader-Willi syndrome causes childhood hyperphagia and obesity.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The congenital near-total absence of subcutaneous fat is the decisive discriminator. The metabolic consequences then reinforce, rather than create, the diagnosis.
